stations.title: Load 12 cells
stations.does: Load 12 cylindrical cells from a tray into the module frame on the carrier.
steps: Detect incoming carrier ID and confirm correct module frame orientation.
Pick and place 12 cylindrical cells into the 12 cell seats of the plastic module frame (top/end aligned to tooling datum).
Verify each cell is seated to depth using seat-stop contact sensors (pass/fail per seat).
Wait for all seat confirmations; then release the carrier to the next station.

stations.title: Place copper busbars
stations.does: Lay the copper busbars onto the tops of the installed cells.
steps: Detect carrier and busbar kit availability (busbars staged for orientation-specific positions).
Pick the required busbar set and place each busbar onto the designated cell-top position.
Use a guided fixture or push-in datum to seat busbar edges flush on the cell tops (no sliding).
Run a brief presence check for each busbar location (photo-eye/contact sensor).
Release the carrier to the next station when all busbars are confirmed present.

stations.title: Laser-weld busbars
stations.does: Laser-weld each busbar to the corresponding cell terminals.
steps: Clamp/locate the carrier within the laser-weld enclosure tooling datum.
For each weld point: focus laser, fire pulse sequence, and confirm weld cycle complete (cycle time / interlock OK).
Do not release the carrier until all planned weld points for the 12-cell module are finished.
Open tooling and release carrier to the test station.

stations.title: Test & pass/reject
stations.does: Perform voltage and insulation testing; route failed modules to a reject lane and let passed modules proceed.
steps: Clamp/position the carrier contacts for test across all relevant cell terminals/busbar nodes.
Apply voltage/insulation test routine and collect results (voltage OK, insulation OK thresholds).
Decide result: if any fail -> mark FAIL; else mark PASS.
If PASS: apply pass label/mark on the carrier and send to main exit conveyor position.
If FAIL: apply reject label/mark and divert carrier to the physical reject lane position.

notes: Each station is budgeted ≤ 180 s takt (takt = 3600/20 = 180 s). If your real laser-weld cycle or end-of-line test time is longer than assumed, the bottleneck station may need parallelization or additional takt allowance limited to the takt.
Reject lane implementation is assumed to be handled as a built-in diversion at ST4; if it requires a separate downstream station, confirm the physical layout and diversion method.
Busbar count and exact weld-point mapping are assumed to be handled entirely by ST2/ST3 tooling; confirm if the cycle must vary busbar variants per module.
